Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D plus probiotic co-supplementation lowered Beck Depression Inventory scores compared with placebo in women with PCOS.
Sentence: "Vitamin D and probiotic co-supplementation, compared with the placebo, significantly improved beck depression inventory [β (difference in the mean of outcomes measures between treatment groups) - 0.58; 95% CI, - 1.15, - 0.02; P = 0.04], general health questionnaire scores (β - 0.93; 95% CI, - 1.78, - 0.08; P = 0.03) and depression, anxiety and stress scale scores (β - 0.90; 95% CI, - 1.67, - 0.13; P = 0.02)."
Measured as: beck depression inventory score
Population: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome aged 18-40 years
Intervention: 50,000 IU vitamin D every 2 weeks plus 8 × 10^9 CFU/day probiotic for 12 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 60
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: Patients with cognitive impairment had lower NPI dysphoria/depression scores (fewer symptoms) than cognitively normal patients.
Sentence: "On the NPI, the CI group had significantly lower scores (indicating fewer symptoms) than the CN group across all 12 domains, including delusions, hallucinations, agitation/aggression, dysphoria/depression, anxiety, elation/euphoria, apathy/indifference, disinhibition, irritability/lability, aberrant motor activity, nighttime behaviours/sleep disturbances, and appetite/eating disorders, as well as higher total NPI scores (p < 0.05)."
Measured as: NPI dysphoria/depression domain score
Population: Patients with ESRD undergoing maintenance haemodialysis
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (measured, not given)
Comparator: Cognitively normal group vs cognitively impaired group
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 132
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study B compares cognitively impaired vs normal haemodialysis patients on NPI scores, and vitamin D is only a measured covariate, not the exposure contrasted, so it is not a vitamin D comparison.","verdict":"off_question","reason":null,"also_differs":[],"detail":"exposure: cognitive impairment status (CI vs CN group), not vitamin D"}
